videos.script: Rui's team runs seventy message flows. Ask him what one of them does, and he describes its nodes. {{nodes}} An input node. A Compute node. A Route node. Something called AggregateControl, and its partner, AggregateReply. That is how the flow is built. It is not what the flow does. {{sentence}} In 2003 Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf gave this work a vocabulary. Sixty-five patterns, each with a name and an icon. {{icons}} With it, the same flow fits in one sentence. Translate the supermarket's order. Split it per store. Send each part to the system that sells it. Gather the replies into one answer. {{flow}} This lesson teaches the vocabulary as a tool, not a list to memorise. You use it to read flows somebody else built, and to describe your own. And you use it to review. Each name comes with a question. An aggregator: when is it finished? An enricher: what does it call, and how many times? {{review}} Joana asks those questions of the order flow, which has run every morning since 2016. Two of the answers are ones nobody wanted to hear.
